meta.title: East regional distribution center: close in 2027, or retain and optimize?
meta.subtitle: CEO and board decision paper · Board meeting pre-read, November 2026
meta.purpose: Decide whether to close the East regional distribution center in 2027 or retain and optimize it
meta.confidentiality: Based only on the board briefing pack (synthetic case data). All figures in US$, at 2027 volumes unless stated

inputs.label: Northline Home board briefing pack (synthetic case data)
Finished analysis deck, extracted to text (the source of truth for this compile)

storyline.governing_thought: Retain and optimize East through its 2029 lease end and test the cross-dock: closing saves at most $0.10M a year, not $1.3M, and fails or cannot yet prove the board's tests

exec_summary.text: Closing East does not pay once routing and handling are counted

sub_points.text: Serving East from Central nets $0.10M a year, not the $1.3M claimed, and zero at 2028 volume, before the $0.75M exit fee
The cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today: $0.60M of extra transport outweighs $0.45M of fixed cost removed
Optimized retention (K) is cheapest in the base case: $8.44M in 2027, $0.20–0.45M a year below either closure

exec_summary.text: Closure also breaks, or cannot yet prove, the board's binding constraints

sub_points.text: Close to Central: 90.3% against the 92% contract; Central at 100% in 2027 and 108% in 2028; $1.85M one-time with its unbudgeted retrofit, against $0.9M
Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, but from a six-week, non-holiday pilot with no all-ZIP definition and no promotion guarantee
Retain and optimize: 95.1% network rate, Central at 47% of capacity in 2028, and $0.15M one-time

exec_summary.text: Optimize now, test the cross-dock, and decide the 2029 lease at a Q3 2028 gate

sub_points.text: Approve Option K and a cross-dock test capped at $0.25M through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, measured on all ZIP codes
Waiting avoids the $0.75M exit fee and settles whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited, a swing of $0.85M a year
Drop close-to-Central: its $5-per-order penalty makes it no cheaper than today at 2028 volume, even if Central were expanded

next_steps.action: Keep East open in 2027 and approve Option K ($0.15M one-time)
Authorize a cross-dock test of up to $0.25M with an all-ZIP SLA and no two-year minimum, subject to provider agreement
Renegotiate East shifts, set up the SKU transfer buffer, track East's all-ZIP rate weekly against 95%
Run the cross-dock test through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, including rural ZIPs
Take the 2029 lease decision against the four gate criteria

lead_message.text: We judged four designs and a deferral path on the board's four tests plus reversibility, using all-in cost and all-ZIP service

slides.rationale: Options set against the criteria they are judged on: two contrasting columns (source: two lists)

columns.header: Four network designs and a deferral path
detail: **SQ, status quo:** keep all three sites as they are today; the reference case
**K, retain and optimize:** renegotiate East staffing shifts and add a transfer buffer for low-volume SKUs; saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M upfront
**C, close East and serve from Central:** end the East lease in 2027 ($0.75M) and ship all 200k Eastern orders from Central at $13 each
**X, close East and use a cross-dock:** a two-year third-party deal at $11 per order plus a $0.85M annual minimum
**D, defer (middle path):** run K now, test the cross-dock through holiday peak, and decide at the 2029 lease end

columns.header: Five tests: four set by the board, plus reversibility
detail: **1 Economics:** lowest all-in annual cost (transport, facility fixed cost, damage) plus one-time cost, not the CFO's carrier-only cost per shipment
**2 Service:** at least 92% of all orders delivered within two days, network-wide, on all ZIP codes; the contracted KPI, not the ex-rural dashboard
**3 Capacity:** Central at or below its 360k certified practical capacity in 2027 and under 2028 growth (East +10%, Central +6%)
**4 Funding and lease:** no more than $0.9M of one-time change cost in 2027; East early exit $0.75M; West lease fixed to 2030
**5 Risk:** decision-grade evidence and reversibility; rebuilding East-type capacity takes nine months

slides.so_what: Closure is hard to reverse, so it must pass all five tests on today's evidence; a gap is a risk, not a pass
footnotes: Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 2, 3, 6.

lead_message.text: The CEO's 'keep East open in 2027' held up under testing, but it needed three refinements

slides.rationale: Five conditions, each with evidence and a verdict -> table; the refined answer reads it in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **Hypothesis tested (CEO's view):** keep East open in 2027, because Central lacks spare capacity for growth

bullets: **Retain and optimize, not just retain:** Option K beats the status quo by $0.30M a year at low risk
**Capacity rules out only close-to-Central:** the cross-dock fails on cost, $0.45M a year above K in the base case, and on unproven peak service
**Keep East through 2029, not permanently:** the exit fee falls away at lease end; test the cross-dock now and decide at a Q3 2028 gate

rows.label: a  Closing saves little once all costs count

cells.text: C nets $0.10M a year, not $1.3M, and $0 at 2028 volume; X costs $0.15M a year more than today

rows.label: b  Closing puts the 92% SLA at risk

cells.text: C: 90.3% network rate (fail); X: 93.9% on paper, from non-peak pilot data

rows.label: c  Central cannot absorb Eastern demand

cells.text: True for C (108% of capacity in 2028); not relevant to X, which does not use Central

rows.label: d  Keeping East fits the lease and budget

cells.text: Lease runs to 2029 with no fee; K needs $0.15M of the $0.9M authorized

rows.label: e  Keeping East is the cheapest way to the SLA

cells.text: Even unoptimized, East ($8.74M) beats X ($8.89M), the only closure that meets the SLA; K is $8.44M

footnotes: Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 2–7; Northline analysis.

lead_message.text: Five claims in the board pre-read overstate the case for one side or the other and should not anchor the decision

slides.rationale: Claims set against what they leave out and the corrected figure -> comparison table

cells.text: Counts East's fixed cost only; leaves out higher Central-to-East transport (+$5 × 200k), $0.2M extra damage and the $0.75M exit fee
$0.10M a year before the $0.75M exit fee (−$0.65M in 2027); $0 at 2028 volume

rows.label: Cost per shipment as the cost KPI

cells.text: Carrier invoice ÷ orders; excludes warehouse rent, returns and replacements, so it is a transport KPI only
Use all-in cost: $8.44–8.89M a year by option
Excludes rural deliveries; the contract KPI counts every ZIP code
Correlation only: East serves more high-volume accounts with dedicated sales teams, and this is not controlled for
Not usable as causal evidence; retention response to service is unknown

rows.label: “Close in June 2027 and absorb at Central with today's staffing”

cells.text: Puts Central at its full 360k practical load before any demand spike; 2028 growth takes it past capacity

slides.so_what: The corrections cut both ways: they shrink the closure saving and the service and loyalty case for East
footnotes: Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 3, 5. Corrected figures: Northline analysis.

lead_message.text: After routing and damage costs, the CFO's $1.3M closure saving shrinks to $0.10M a year, and to zero at 2028 volume

slides.rationale: What takes the claimed saving down to the net -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **Option C (close East, serve from Central): annual saving compared with the status quo**, $M, 2027

sidebar.header: At 2028 volume the saving is gone
sidebar.caption: thousand Eastern orders a year at which it reaches zero, ($1.30M − $0.20M) ÷ $5: exactly the 2028 forecast
bullets: **Not yet included, and all make it worse:** the $0.75M exit fee, a 7.5-year payback at $0.10M a year for a lease that ends in 2029 anyway
**Also unpriced:** the carrier surcharge needed to lift Eastern service above 84%, and the $1.1M Central retrofit 2028 growth needs
**Against Option K:** close-to-Central costs $0.20M a year more even before these items

footnotes: Transport rates exclude facility cost, damage and the exit charge. 2028: Eastern volume +10% to 220k; the 20k extra orders cost $5 more each.

lead_message.text: Under the base reading of the cross-dock quote, optimized retention (K) is the cheapest all-in design in 2027 and 2028

slides.rationale: Totals by option, then the gap to K by year -> two column panels (source: build-up table and gap chart)

panels.header: K has the lowest all-in cost of the four designs in both years
Both closures cost more than K every year, and their gap widens in 2028 as each extra Eastern order costs $3–5 more

slides.so_what: Over 2027–28, K is $0.45M cheaper than the status quo even after its $0.15M setup cost
footnotes: Two-year totals incl. one-time cost: SQ $17.73M, K $17.28M, C $18.38M, X $18.84M. K's $0.30M saving is set against facility cost; build-up in the appendix.
C excludes the unpriced carrier surcharge and the $1.1M retrofit. 2028: East +10%, Central +6%, West flat.

lead_message.text: Closure beats optimized retention only below 160k Eastern orders, against 200k in 2027 and 220k forecast for 2028

slides.rationale: Saving as a function of volume, two options -> two lines crossing zero at their break-evens
slides.unit_line: **Annual saving of each closure option compared with Option K, by Eastern volume**, $M, thousand Eastern orders a year

sidebar.header: Closure loses at every plausible volume
sidebar.caption: thousand Eastern orders a year: only below this would close-to-Central beat K
bullets: **Close to Central:** breaks even with K at 160k and with the status quo at 220k orders
**Cross-dock:** zero at 50k against K and 150k against the status quo; at 200k it costs $0.15M a year more than today
**Lower growth does not rescue closure:** volume would have to fall 20% (C) or 75% (X)

footnotes: Saving against K: C = ($1.30M − $0.30M − $0.20M) − $5 × orders; X = ($1.30M − $0.30M − $0.85M) − $3 × orders. K's $0.30M is lost if East closes.
One-time costs excluded; assumes rates and fixed costs do not change with volume.

lead_message.text: Serving East from Central breaches the contracted 92% SLA; the cross-dock clears it on paper by 1.9 percentage points

slides.rationale: Margin of each option against one floor -> bars, kept in option order
slides.unit_line: **Network-wide two-day delivery rate compared with the 92% contract floor**, percentage points, 2027

sidebar.caption: minimum Eastern all-ZIP two-day rate that keeps the network at 92%
bullets: **Close to Central (84%):** 4.3 percentage points short; about 8,600 orders a year fall short, triggering retailer penalty clauses
**Cross-dock pilot (93%):** 4.7 percentage points of headroom, but on non-peak data with an unstated measurement basis
**Retaining East (96%):** 7.7 percentage points of headroom

basis.header: How the network rate is built: close-to-Central case

terms.caption: k Central and West on time (94%, 95%)

footnotes: Central and West keep their 94% and 95%. East's 96% is all-ZIP; the basis of the 84% (modeled) and the 93% (pilot) is not stated.
Finance's 98% (ex-rural) and the dashboard are not the contract KPI. C's 84% rises only with an unpriced carrier surcharge, widening its $0.20M gap to K.
Threshold = (460.0k − 283.4k) ÷ 200k: on-time orders needed for 92% of 500k, less Central and West on time, over Eastern orders.

lead_message.text: The cross-dock's 93% comes from a short, non-peak pilot with an unstated measurement basis and no promotion guarantee

slides.rationale: Three facts about one piece of evidence -> KPI tiles (source: four tiles; the two non-numeric ones are driver lines here)
slides.unit_line: **Cross-dock pilot behind the 93% two-day rate**, six-week pilot excluding holiday weeks

items.caption: of annual Eastern volume tested
drivers: 12,000 pilot orders, against 200k Eastern orders a year
A full-year rate is a weighted average, so a short non-peak sample can overstate it

items.caption: weeks of pilot, with no holiday weeks
drivers: Holiday weeks were excluded from the pilot
Peak weeks carry the most service risk

items.caption: two-day rate in the pilot, on an unstated basis
drivers: The quote does not say whether the 93% covers all ZIP codes
The operator has not guaranteed service during the national spring promotion
The provider would accept termination for cause if the contract defines all-ZIP service

lead_message.text: The cross-dock needs a holiday-peak, all-ZIP test to show its 4.7 percentage points of headroom are real

slides.rationale: Sensitivity grid of the pilot rate stays a grid; the test criteria read it in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **How much headroom the pilot really gives**, Eastern and network two-day rates, 2027

sidebar.header: What a decision-grade test must show (proposed)
bullets: **Coverage:** holiday peak 2027 and the spring 2028 promotion, including rural ZIPs
**Service:** at least 92% all-ZIP over the full test and at least 90% in peak weeks, keeping the network at or above 93.5%
**Contract:** an all-ZIP SLA, a termination-for-cause clause, and clarity on whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited
**Cost:** a measured damage and handling rate on transshipped goods

rows.label: If the pilot excluded rural ZIPs (−2 pp)

terms.caption: East's ex-rural 98% against its all-ZIP 96% (briefing pack)
Eastern rate if the pilot excluded rural ZIPs

slides.so_what: Weak peak weeks could erase the remaining 3–5 percentage points of headroom after the minimum is signed
footnotes: The 2 pp gap is illustrative only. Test thresholds are proposed by Northline analysis, not taken from the pack.

lead_message.text: Close-to-Central would fill Central to 100% of capacity from day one and 108% in 2028; even lower growth does not fit

slides.rationale: Load against a fixed capacity by case -> columns with the capacity as a dashed line
slides.unit_line: **Central hub annual shipments compared with its 360k certified practical capacity**, thousands

bullets: **2028 forecast:** 169.6k Central plus 220k Eastern orders is 29.6k over capacity; only zero growth fits, at exactly 100%
**The fix does not fit the plan:** expansion needs a two-quarter permit and a $1.1M retrofit that is not in the 2027 budget
**K and X add no load:** capacity is not a reason to reject them

terms.caption: thousand orders at Central under C, 14.8k over capacity

footnotes: Operations: absorbing East with today's staffing (the consultant's June 2027 plan) puts Central at full practical load before any demand spike.
The pack asks for a lower-growth case to be discussed but does not size it; half the forecast is the analysis's illustrative choice.

lead_message.text: Retention and deferral fit the $0.9M one-time authority; close-to-Central fits only if its $1.1M retrofit stays unfunded

slides.rationale: One-time cost by option against one authority -> columns with the authority as a dashed line
slides.unit_line: **One-time network change cost by option**, $M, 2027, against the board's $0.9M authority

bullets: **East:** exit in 2027 costs a one-time $0.75M, otherwise the lease expires in 2029; waiting avoids the fee, so 2029 is the natural point to decide
**West:** cannot change before 2030; outside this decision
**Central:** fixed cost unchanged in every option; expansion needs a permit and an unbudgeted $1.1M retrofit, to be budgeted for 2028 or later
**Cross-dock:** a two-year minimum at $0.85M a year locks in about $1.7M before peak service is proven

footnotes: C's $1.85M = $0.75M exit + $1.1M retrofit; without it C leaves $0.15M for customer migration, and a two-quarter permit misses a June 2027 closure.
The board rule against degrading service for a freight discount limits closing C's cost gap with cheaper, slower carriers.
The $0.25M test cap is an assumption pending a provider quote.

lead_message.text: Only K and D pass all five tests: the cross-dock fails on cost and is unproven on service; close-to-Central fails four

slides.rationale: Options compared on the same five tests -> comparison table, the recommended rows highlighted

cells.text: FAIL: $0.30M a year dearer than K
PASS: K's cost; ≤$0.25M buys the option
FAIL: +$0.45M a year against K (base case)
FAIL: two-year minimum; nine months to reverse
FAIL: +$0.20M a year against K; $0 saving against SQ by 2028

slides.so_what: K and D pass today; D also buys a cheap cross-dock option for the 2029 lease, so D is the recommended path
footnotes: 'Unproven' counts as a fail until a peak test is complete. Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 2–7; Northline analysis.

lead_message.text: The cross-dock's economics swing by $0.85M a year on one open question: is its minimum a fee or a credited floor

slides.rationale: Two readings by two years stays a grid, drawn as clustered bars (positive = costs more than K)
slides.unit_line: **Cross-dock annual all-in cost compared with Option K**, $M (positive = costs more than K)

sidebar.header: Reading A is the base case: the pack lists the $0.85M under fixed facility cost
bullets: **Reading A, a fee on top of $11 per order:** the cross-dock costs more than K every year and is never worth closing East for at forecast volumes
**Reading B, a spend floor credited against charges:** it would save $0.40M a year against K in 2027 and $0.34M in 2028, worth it only if peak all-ZIP service is proven
**Settle it before signing:** the test contract must state whether the minimum is extra or credited

footnotes: Reading B is a sensitivity, not the base case. Under it the cross-dock costs $8.04M in 2027 and $8.35M in 2028, against K's $8.44M and $8.69M.
Inputs: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 3 and 6; Reading B is the analysis's sensitivity.

lead_message.text: Waiting for the 2029 lease end costs little and answers the one contract question that could make the cross-dock pay

slides.rationale: What the middle path costs and buys -> value table; why waiting wins reads it in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **What the deferral path costs and buys**

sidebar.header: Waiting beats closing now, even under Reading B
bullets: **Closing in 2027 gains little:** under Reading B, $0.40M + $0.34M − $0.75M exit + $0.15M of K setup avoided = $0.14M over two years
**Waiting avoids the early-exit fee:** the lease ends in 2029, so the $0.75M charge falls away (transfer costs within it may remain)
**The downside is lopsided:** each percentage point of Eastern service below 88.3% adds 2,000 late orders a year and pushes the network below 92%, with penalties and nine months to reverse

rows.label: Early-exit fee avoided by waiting to 2029
Cross-dock minimums not committed before proof

slides.so_what: Close-to-Central is dropped, not deferred: it loses to K at any volume above 160k
footnotes: The ≤$0.25M test cost is an assumption pending a provider quote. Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 3, 6, 7.

lead_message.text: Three steps: optimize East now, test the cross-dock through peak and promotion, then decide the lease at a Q3 2028 gate

slides.rationale: Phases with dates and an exit gate -> process flow; the decisions asked today read it in the sidebar

sidebar.header: Decisions requested from the board today
bullets: **1:** Keep East open in 2027; do not serve the East region from Central
**2:** Approve Option K ($0.15M one-time)
**3:** Authorize a cross-dock test of up to $0.25M with an all-ZIP SLA and no two-year minimum (subject to provider agreement)
**4:** Schedule the 2029 lease gate for Q3 2028

detail: Approve $0.15M for systems changes
Renegotiate East shifts; set up the low-volume SKU transfer buffer
Guardrail: East all-ZIP two-day rate at or above 95%, tracked weekly
Confirm East can handle 220k orders in 2028
Test contract: all-ZIP SLA, termination for cause, how the minimum is treated
Route a sample of Eastern orders, incl. rural ZIPs, through holiday 2027 and spring 2028
Measure all-ZIP rate, peak weeks, damage and cost per order
Close East at lease end only if all four hold:
Service: ≥92% all-ZIP over the test, ≥90% in peak weeks
Network SLA (modeled): ≥93.5%, a 1.5 pp buffer
Cost: at least $0.2M a year below K at forecast volume
Contract: all-ZIP SLA, termination for cause, budget fit

footnotes: Either way, transition before the 2029 expiry; confirm the expiry date leaves at least six months after the gate. Gate thresholds are proposals.
Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 6, 7; Northline analysis.

lead_message.text: The recommendation holds under the main uncertainties: each one has a monitoring trigger and a planned response

slides.rationale: Risks set against their effect and trigger -> table

rows.label: K's $0.30M saving does not materialize (audit estimate)

cells.text: Still right: the status quo ($8.74M) beats X ($8.89M), and C fails the SLA and capacity tests regardless
Track savings quarterly; stop shift changes if service suffers
Headroom of 7.7 pp on the Eastern rate (96% against 88.3%)
Weekly all-ZIP tracking; act if East drops below 95%

rows.label: Growth falls short (marketplace promotion not contracted)

cells.text: Closure still loses: 2027 volume is already 200k, above every break-even except C against SQ (220k)
Rerun break-evens at the gate with actual volumes
East site capacity is not in the pack; 220k is assumed to fit
Confirm East capacity in the Q1 2027 audit

rows.label: Customer retention response to service is unknown

cells.text: Not used: the 92% floor binds regardless; Marketing's 8 pp claim is confounded
Controlled renewal analysis by account size and sales coverage

rows.label: Cross-dock peak service, damage rate and terms are unknown

cells.text: Exactly what the test resolves; no commitment before the gate
Gate criteria on the plan page
Matters only for close-to-Central, which is dropped

footnotes: Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 4, 5, 7; Northline analysis.

lead_message.text: Cost model detail: every option is built from the same rates, volumes and fixed costs in the briefing pack

slides.unit_line: **Annual cost by line item and option**, $M, 2027 and 2028
footnotes: Basis: East-region $8 (SQ, K), $13 (C), $11 (X) per order; Central orders × $9; West 140k × $10; East fixed $1.30M, K −$0.30M; Central $1.80M + West $1.20M.
Minimum $0.85M a year (Reading A; Reading B credits it); C damage $0.20M held flat; one-time: systems $0.15M, exit $0.75M. 2028 = East 220k, Central 169.6k.
Not modeled (no figure in the pack): C's carrier surcharge, retrofit timing, returns and replacements, penalties, Central's 94% under full load. Totals may not add.
Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 3, 4, 6.

lead_message.text: Analyst choices made without client input, each stated so the board can challenge it

cells.text: Treated as a fixed fee on top of $11 per order (Reading A)
Listed under fixed facility cost. Under Reading B the cross-dock would be $0.34–0.40M a year cheaper than K, but still unproven on service: this is why we test, not close
Reduction of East facility and operating cost
Scaling would make C worse by $0.02M
Stay at 94% and 95% in every option
Generous to C: Central at 100% load would probably slip
No test quote in the pack (only a two-year minimum); needs provider agreement
The pack asks for one but does not size it; capacity fails at any growth above zero
Expiry month not given; allows six or more months to transition

footnotes: These choices were made because the pack is silent or ambiguous; none changes the recommendation except where noted. Source: briefing pack, sections 2–7.

compile.source: evidence/analysis.md: finished 18-slide CEO and board decision paper, extracted to text; built from evidence/briefing-pack.md

units.text: Retain and optimize East through its 2029 lease end, and use 2027–28 to test the cross-dock alternative before the lease decision
Approve Option K: saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M one-time
Authorize a cross-dock test of up to $0.25M (assumption) with an all-ZIP SLA and no two-year minimum, through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, subject to provider agreement
Keep East open in 2027; do not serve the East region from Central. Close-to-Central is dropped, not deferred
Schedule the 2029 lease gate for Q3 2028; close East at lease end only if all four gate criteria are met, otherwise renew
The CFO's $1.3M is East's gross fixed cost; close-to-Central nets $0.10M a year, zero at 2028 volume, before the $0.75M exit fee (7.5-year payback)
The cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today: $0.60M of extra transport against $0.45M of fixed cost removed
Under the base reading, K is the cheapest all-in design in 2027 ($8.44M) and 2028; $0.20–0.45M a year below either closure
K is $0.45M cheaper than the status quo over 2027–28 after its $0.15M setup; the gap to closures widens with volume
Closure beats K only below 160k Eastern orders (C) or 50k (X); 2027 volume is already 200k; volume would have to fall 20% or 75%
Network two-day rate: C 90.3% (fails 92%; about 8,600 orders short), X 93.9% on paper, K 95.1%
Minimum Eastern all-ZIP rate that keeps the network at 92% is 88.3%
The cross-dock's 93% is from a six-week, 12,000-order (6%) non-holiday pilot with unstated measurement basis and no promotion guarantee; needs a peak, all-ZIP test
Pilot headroom 4.7 pp as reported, 2.7 pp if the pilot excluded rural ZIPs (illustrative); peak weeks could erase the rest
Gate criteria: ≥92% all-ZIP over the test and ≥90% in peak weeks; network ≥93.5%; cross-dock ≥$0.2M a year below K; all-ZIP SLA, termination for cause, budget fit / treatment of the minimum
Under C, Central runs at 100% of capacity in 2027 and 108% in 2028; even the lower-growth case does not fit; K or X leave Central at 47%
Expansion needs a two-quarter permit and a $1.1M retrofit not in the 2027 budget; C's one-time cost incl. retrofit is $1.85M against $0.9M
One-time cost: K $0.15M, D $0.40M, X $0.75M ($0.15M spare), all within the $0.9M authority
East exit in 2027 costs $0.75M, otherwise the lease expires in 2029; West fixed to 2030; signing the cross-dock locks in about $1.7M of minimums
Reading B (minimum credited) makes the cross-dock $0.40M (2027) and $0.34M (2028) cheaper than K; the reading swings its economics by $0.85M a year; Reading A is the base case
Waiting beats closing now: under Reading B closing in 2027 gains only $0.14M over two years; the exit fee falls away at 2029; each point below 88.3% adds 2,000 late orders a year
Five pre-read claims overstate one side or the other (CFO $1.3M, cost per shipment, Finance 98%, Marketing 8 percentage points, consultant's June 2027 plan) and cut both ways
The CEO's 'keep East open' hypothesis held but needed three refinements: optimize, capacity rules out only C, keep East through 2029 not permanently
Only K and D pass all five tests; X fails on cost and risk and is unproven on service; C fails four tests; D is the recommended path
The recommendation holds under seven uncertainties, each with a trigger and response (K saving, shift changes, growth short or above, retention, cross-dock unknowns, permit timing)
Four designs and a deferral path judged on five tests (board's four plus reversibility), all-in cost and all-ZIP service; burden of proof on closure
Analyst choices where the pack is silent (Reading A, damage held flat, Central and West service held, test cap, lower-growth case, gate timing)
Cost model line items for every option, 2027 and 2028, and items not modeled
Guardrail: East all-ZIP two-day rate at or above 95%, tracked weekly, during the shift renegotiation
Three steps with timing: optimize East Q1–Q2 2027; test Q2 2027 – Q2 2028; board gate Q3 2028, transition before the 2029 expiry
C's 84% can be lifted only with a carrier surcharge not in the $13 rate; the board will not degrade service for a freight discount
